newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany says G7 already working on Lima crisis.
newsitem.headline: Germany says G7 already working on Lima crisis.

text.p: Germany said on Friday Group of Seven countries were working together on plans to help resolve the 10-day-old Peru hostage crisis.
Foreign Ministry spokesman Martin Erdmann told Reuters that G7 ambassadors had already met in Lima to discuss their next step. He said that Russia was also taking part in the talks.
"The main objective is to prevent violence," Erdmann said.
The German statement came after Japan called on fellow G7 nations to help it hammer out a joint solution to the crisis.
Erdmann said that even though all the German hostages had been freed, Germany was still taking part in the crisis management.
He added the German government has had no contact with Isaac Velazco, a Hamburg-based self-styled international spokesman for the Tupac Amaru Revoluntary Movement (MRTA).
Marxist MRTA rebels are holding 104 VIP hostages in the Japanese ambassador's residency in Lima in a siege now in its tenth day.

Velazco, who said he was granted political asylum in Germany in 1994 after fleeing Peru in November 1993, told Reuters by telephone that MRTA had successfully achieved its first aim of drawing world attention to its beliefs.
He said it was now concentrating on obtaining the freedom of its militants behind from jails in Peru.
